english: "Just what," one may ask, "do you mean when you mention types of deeds that are certain to ripen?" acip: ZHING GI KHYAD PAR LAS MTHONG CHOS 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LAS SU 'GYUR PA NI, SDON BDAG CAG GI STON PA DGE SLONG SDE SNOD GSUM PAR GYUR PA NA, DGE 'DUN GYIS RTZOD PA 'PHEL BAR BYAS PA DGE SLONG SDE SNOD 'DZIN PA ZHIG GIS BSDUMS PAS, DGE SLONG SDE SNOD GSUM PA DE KHROS NAS BUD MED KYIS BUD MED KYI RTZOD PA ZHI BAR BYAS SO ZHES SKUR PA BTAB PA LAS, TSE DE NYID LA BUD MED DU GYUR CING , DE NAS SKYE BA LNGA BRGYAR BUD MED DU GYUR PA LTA BU 'O,
wylie: zhing gi khyad par las mthong chos 'bras bu can gyi las su 'gyur pa ni, sdon bdag cag gi ston pa dge slong sde snod gsum par gyur pa na, dge 'dun gyis rtsod pa 'phel bar byas pa dge slong sde snod 'dzin pa zhig gis bsdums pas, dge slong sde snod gsum pa de khros nas bud med kyis bud med kyi rtsod pa zhi bar byas so zhes skur pa btab pa las, tshe de nyid la bud med du gyur cing , de nas skye ba lnga brgyar bud med du gyur pa lta bu 'o
english: A case of a deed which, because of the special features of the object involved, turned into the type that gives a result in the very same life would be as follows. In one of his former lives, our Teacher was once a certain monk who had mastered all three sections of the canon. There had been a steady increase in quarreling among the community of monks. One monk--who had himself committed the sections of the canon to memory--managed to bring the different sides to an agreement. This angered the other monk (the one who was a master of the canon), who made the sarcastic statement that "A woman has settled a women's quarrel." Because of this deed the monk turned into a woman in that very life, and took five hundred births thereafter as a woman as well.

acip: ,BSAM PA'I KHYAD PAR LAS MTHONG CHOS 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LAS SU 'GYUR PA NI, RGYAL PO KA NI KA'I NYUG RUM PA LONG BA ZHES PAS, MI ZHIG GIS GLANG LNGA BRGYA 'DOD PA LA CI BYED DRIS PAS, 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PA YIN ZER LA, SNYING RDZES DE DAG DE LAS THAR PAS BYAS PAS TSE DE NYID LA MTSAN SOR CHUD PA LTA BU'O,
wylie: bsam pa'i khyad par las mthong chos 'bras bu can gyi las su 'gyur pa ni, rgyal po ka ni ka'i nyug rum pa long ba zhes pas, mi zhig gis glang lnga brgya 'dod pa la ci byed dris pas, 'bras bu 'byin pa yin zer la, snying rdzes de dag de las thar pas byas pas tshe de nyid la mtshan sor chud pa lta bu'o
english: An instance of a deed which, because of special features of the thought involved, turns into the type that gives a result that you see in this very life would be as follows. King Kanaka had a certain eunuch by the name of "Longwa." He met someone driving a herd of five hundred cattle and asked the man what he planned to do. "We're going to castrate them," was the reply. Overcome with compassion, Longwa managed to save all the cattle from their fate: as a result, his own organ was restored in the very same life.
